# Wisdom of Solomon Chapter 15 — The EMET Bible (Literal)

**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Codex Vaticanus, Wisdom 15 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/WIS_015_page_001.jpg

---

**15:1** But you, our God, are kind and true, long-suffering, and governing all things in mercy.

**15:2** For even if we sin, we are yours, knowing your might; but we will not sin, knowing that we are reckoned as yours.

**15:3** For to know you is perfect righteousness, and to know your might is the root of immortality.

**15:4** For neither did the evil device of men lead us astray, nor the fruitless toil of painters, a form besmeared with varied colors,

**15:5** the sight of which entices fools into desire, and they long for the breathless form of a dead image.

**15:6** Lovers of evil things and worthy of such hopes are those who make, desire, and worship such things.

**15:7** For a potter, kneading soft earth, laboriously molds each vessel for our service; and from the same clay he fashions both the vessels that serve clean uses and those of opposite kind, all alike; but which shall be the use of each of these is for the potter himself to determine.

**15:8** And with a miserable toil he forms from the same clay a vain god — he who was made of earth a little before, and after a little while goes to the same earth from which he was taken, when the debt of his soul is demanded back.

**15:9** But his concern is not that he will labor, nor that his life is short; but he competes with the goldsmith and silversmith, and he imitates the moulder of bronze, and considers it glory that he molds counterfeits.

**15:10** His heart is ashes, and his hope is cheaper than dirt, and his life is more dishonorable than clay,

**15:11** because he has not known the one who formed him, and the one who breathed into him an active soul and inspired a living spirit.

**15:12** But he has reckoned our life as a plaything, and our existence a bazaar for gain; for he says one must get gain however one can, even from evil.

**15:13** For this man above all others knows that he is sinning, who from earthy stuff makes fragile vessels and graven images.

**15:14** But most foolish of all, and more wretched than the soul of a child, are all the enemies of your people, who oppressed them.

**15:15** For they considered all the idols of the nations as gods, which have neither use of eyes for seeing, nor nostrils for drawing breath, nor ears for hearing, nor fingers of hands for touching, and their feet are useless for walking.

**15:16** For a man made them, and one whose spirit is borrowed shaped them; for no man is able to shape a god like himself.

**15:17** For since he is mortal, what he creates with lawless hands is dead; for he is better than the things he worships, since he has had life, but they never have.

**15:18** Moreover they worship even the most loathsome living creatures; for compared in senselessness these are worse than the rest,

**15:19** and they are not fine-looking enough that one might desire them; yet the creatures have been missed and praised by God.
